title: ST0064 asserts one daemon predicate structurally and nothing observes it at run time
body:
**ST0064's nine criteria are ALL structural, so nothing on the thread asserts that the app EXECUTES the predicate it is built around and USES the answer.** Measured 2026-09-08 by reading all nine, not by inference from one.

`AC-01.2` requires app and CLI to be one predicate reached through one code path. `AC-01.6` requires the three endpoint states to be a projection above `route()`, and argues in its own text that this makes `AC-01.2` true **by construction**. `one_daemon_predicate_across_both_trees.rs` discharges the static half well: no SECOND predicate is *spelled* in the app target, controlled both ways -- synthetic input to the pure predicate, plus a live plant carried through the real walk.

**WHAT NO ROW COVERS, IN ic's OWN WORDS, WHICH ARE SHARPER THAN A RESTATEMENT:** *an app that shells the CLI verb and then ignores its answer passes here and is exactly as broken as the case the row forbids.* A static read cannot watch a process. The type system proves `route()` is total; the static check proves nothing else is spelled; neither observes execution.

**AND IT IS NOT `AC-01.4`'s.** That row is the tail-orphan trap -- driving the app open and shut and reading `ps`, against SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGKILL separately, because a log pipeline behind a runtime leaks a `tail` per open-and-close. It is a live drive of a DIFFERENT claim. Delegating the run-time half to it would be a hand-off the row does not accept.

**THE REASON THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN WRITTEN INTO A MODULE DOC:** a hand-off to a row that does not accept it is worse than a stated gap, because the gap is visible and the hand-off is not -- a reader follows the pointer, finds a row about `tail` processes, and either re-derives the whole question or assumes they misread. But an uncovered clause recorded ONLY in a Rust module doc is invisible to the gate, which is the silent-exclusion shape this estate keeps finding. Filing is what makes it visible without minting a contract row on a node's own initiative.

**FOR hv, AND IT IS A NARROW QUESTION:** does the run-time half earn a criterion of its own, or is `ST0064` deliberately a structural thread whose run-time assurance lives in `AC-01.4`'s drive plus operator use? Either answer is defensible. What is not defensible is the current state, where the clause is uncovered and nothing says so.

Raised by ic while satisfying `AC-01.2` and `AC-01.6`; ic's preference, which vc shares: *I would rather it read as a gap than as a hand-off nobody accepted.*
